source_text: Historia famosissima: Aegyptus plagis castigata ut Hebraeos libertati redderet. Virga Aaron in draconem absorbuit dracones magorum; tamen induratum est cor Pharaonis. In pluribus plagis dicitur induratum; in aliis induravit Dominus cor Pharaonis. Haec intellectum tenent.
pass_a_gloss: History most-famous: Egypt by-plagues chastised that Hebrews to-liberty it-might-return. Rod of-Aaron into dragon swallowed dragons of-magicians; yet hardened was heart of-Pharaoh. In many plagues is-said hardened; in others hardened Lord heart of-Pharaoh. These understanding hold.
pass_b_english: The story of the [[ten plagues >> Bible:Exodus 7-12]] is known to the whole world: Egypt and Pharaoh are beaten with signs until a freeborn people, forced into slavery, is restored to liberty. Aaron’s rod becomes a serpent and swallows the magicians’ serpents; still [[Pharaoh’s heart was hardened >> Bible:Exodus 7:13]]. Sometimes Scripture says the heart “was hardened,” sometimes [[the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart >> Bible:Exodus 9:12]]. The careful reader must not rush past that difference.
